question.:question/problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=(x + y)\,i+(- x + y)\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i+3 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j$ for $t\in[0,2\pi)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the outward flux is

$$\oint_C F\cdot n\,\mathrm ds=\oint_C P\,\mathrm dy-Q\,\mathrm dx,$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C$.

Along the curve $C$, we have $x=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}$, $y=3 \sin{\left(t \right)}$.

Therefore, $P=3 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}$ and $Q=3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)}$.

Computing the derivatives gives $x\prime(t)=- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)}$ and $y\prime(t)=3 \cos{\left(t \right)}$.

Finally, evaluate the integral:

$$\begin{aligned}\oint_C F\cdot n\,\mathrm ds&=\int_0^{2\pi}(P y\prime-Q x\prime)\,\mathrm dt\\&=\int_0^{2\pi}\left[(3 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 3 \cos{\left(t \right)})(3 \cos{\left(t \right)})-(3 \sin{\left(t \right)} - 3 \cos{\left(t \right)})(- 3 \sin{\left(t \right)})\right]\,\mathrm dt\\&=\int_0^{2\pi}\left(9 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 9 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\,\mathrm dt.\end{aligned}$$

Using $\cos^2t+\sin^2t=1$, the integrand is $9$. Thus the flux is $[9t]_0^{2\pi}=18 \pi$.

question.:question/problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)=(x)\,i+(x + y)\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\,i+8 \sin{\left(t \right)}\,j$ for $t\in[0,2\pi)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the outward flux is

$$\oint_C F\cdot n\,\mathrm ds=\oint_C P\,\mathrm dy-Q\,\mathrm dx,$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C$.

Along the curve $C$, we have $x=2 \cos{\left(t \right)}$, $y=8 \sin{\left(t \right)}$.

Therefore, $P=2 \cos{\left(t \right)}$ and $Q=8 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}$.

Computing the derivatives gives $x\prime(t)=- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)}$ and $y\prime(t)=8 \cos{\left(t \right)}$.

Finally, evaluate the integral:

$$\begin{aligned}\oint_C F\cdot n\,\mathrm ds&=\int_0^{2\pi}(P y\prime-Q x\prime)\,\mathrm dt\\&=\int_0^{2\pi}\left[(2 \cos{\left(t \right)})(8 \cos{\left(t \right)})-(8 \sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)})(- 2 \sin{\left(t \right)})\right]\,\mathrm dt\\&=\int_0^{2\pi}\left(16 \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 4 \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + 16 \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)}\right)\,\mathrm dt.\end{aligned}$$

The integrand is $16+4\sin t\cos t$. Use $u=\sin t$, $\mathrm du=\cos t\,\mathrm dt$ in the second term: $$[16t]_0^{2\pi}+4\int_0^0u\,\mathrm du=32 \pi.$$
